overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no quorum deliberated outside a meeting, and individual site visits and conversations were not meetings. It issued a notice reminder only.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the chairman's May 5, 2012 letter, and his talks with other members, showed deliberation outside a posted meeting about a Wyman Road property.
allegations.key_passage: Although Chairman Bezanson discussed the matter outside of a properly posted meeting with Commissioners Connolly and Norton, these individual conversations did not constitute deliberation under the Open Meeting Law because they did not involve a quorum of the Commission.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged that a quorum of the seven-member Commission deliberated on the property before the May 22, 2012 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find evidence to support the assertion that a quorum of the Commission improperly deliberated in advance of the May 22, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged that the chairman and another member visited the property several times, which they said amounted to a meeting.

allegations.summary: The May 5 letter's promised discussion of the Powers' complaint was not listed in the May 22 meeting notice; the AG issued a reminder only.
allegations.key_passage: Clearly, Chairman Bezanson reasonably anticipated this topic for discussion 48 hours in advance of the meeting, therefore he should have included it in the notice.
